en: The Paramādya Tantra,
the Secret Vajra of Great Bliss,
is the being without beginning or end, Vajrasattva, the one of great delight.
Samantabhadra, you are the self of all; O Vajragarva, you are the Lord, the Lord.
There is no other evil in the three realms equal to dispassion [in its intrinsic nature];
therefore, one should cultivate detachment from sensual desires.
You must not, however, perform what ought not to be done.
Now I shall describe its means of accomplishment, which brings about eternal success,
by which one attains it even in this very life.
The attainment that is eternally perpetual.
From the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga*, through the gathering of Vajrasattva and the songs of Vajradharma.
In [the one] of pure splendor adorned [with ornaments].
In a quadrangular [mandala] with four gates, adorned with turrets and surrounded by railings.
O you who are worshipped by hosts of Vajra-Apsarases!
With its foundation shaped like a crescent moon,
its various peaks stirred by the wind, and resounding with the sound of bells;
In the celestial palace of great bliss (the vajra), which is adorned with necklaces, mirrors, great flowers, garlands, strings of jewels, and ornaments.
He dwelt in great bliss.
The Being without beginning or end,
Vajrasattva, the Great Joy.
Samantabhadra, the self of all, the lord of Vajragarvā, the Lord.
That mind which, because of its firmness, is called "sentient being" (*sattva*) among all beings,
is equal to a vajra due to its concentration; indeed, it is samādhi.
Through certainties, one attains the state of a vajra.
Through the yoga of the empowerment of sentient beings,
one becomes Vajrasattva once again,
beginning with the thorough penetration of one's own mind.
The awakening of the Buddha, according to the prescribed method,
is known as the Tathāgata family;
that very same [awakening] is the pure Padma family.
That indeed is called the noble lineage of jewels.
That very passion is also dispassion; it becomes both desire and liberation;
it is the three times, the three worlds, and the three peaks.
The three worlds, moreover, consist of the three realms.
O you who have transcended all faults,
whose nature is the bliss of universal passion,
grant me the firm heightening of great bliss!
Having practiced and attained accomplishment, bow down quickly.
Brandishing the vajra with pride and maintaining the pride of the vajra, one becomes Vajrasattva himself through the vajras of body, speech, and mind.
In the *Mahāsukhavajraguhya-kalparāja*, samādhi arises from non-conceptuality through the conceptualization for the sake of sentient beings.
By means of that, conceptualization is fully purified, and thus it is called "kalpa."
The lineage of the Tathāgata is that very same [family], and it is remembered as the great Vajra family. (Āmnāyamañjarī)
That very [nature] is the pure Padma family; that itself is said to be the excellent Maṇi family.
For the sake of the welfare of sentient beings, and not for the purification of their own karma, the Victors perform purifications;
herein there is no obstacle, nor indeed are there non-humans.
And in that eon, there is no failure, being sustained by non-increase.
I shall not fall into the state of Māra, nor shall I succumb to lack of firmness;
for the sake of firmness, I shall not teach [the Dharma] out of mere desire for gain.
Rather, I shall quickly become firm for the sake of supreme, excellent enlightenment.
He who would accomplish me through his own pleasures, and not through sufferings.
(The Twentyfold Method: The Union of All Buddhas) Now,
in the delightful primordial realm,
which is established throughout all space:
In [the one] of pure splendor adorned [with ornaments].
In a square [mandala] with four gates, adorned with turrets,
and surrounded by railings—
O you who are worshipped by hosts of Vajra-Apsarases!
With its foundation in the shape of a half-moon,
its various peaks stirred by the wind, and resounding with the sound of bells;
In the celestial palace of great bliss (the Vajra), which is adorned with necklaces, mirrors, great flowers, garlands, and strings of ornaments.
He dwelt in great bliss.
The being without beginning or end,
Vajrasattva, the great delight.
Samantabhadra, the soul of all, the Lord of Vajragarvā, the Lord.
(Vajrāvalī, twenty-fold method:
That mind of all sentient beings is called "sentient being" (*sattva*) because of its firmness.
Through meditative absorption, that which is equal to a vajra (i.e., the meditative absorption) attains the state of a vajra by means of certainties.
Through the yoga of the empowerment of sentient beings,
one becomes Vajrasattva once again;
that indeed is the Tathāgata family.
That itself is known as the Vajra family;
that itself is the pure Padma family; and that itself is said to be the excellent Maṇi family.
That very passion is also dispassion; it becomes both desire and liberation,
the three times, the three realms of existence, and the three peaks.
The three worlds, moreover, consist of the three realms.
(Sarvabuddhasamāyoga) As long as these excellent sages remain here, empowered within existence, [so shall it be].
For that long, the Śākyas, remaining unextinguished, will perform incomparable benefit for sentient beings.
(The Sūtra of Methods:
It is the supreme primordial [mandala] with four gates, [established] by means of the faculties of mindfulness.
It should have four archways;
the meditative concentrations such as Śūraṅgama, Khagañja, and others are known as the railings.
From that [deity] who possesses a multitude of female attendants holding books and other items, their hands busily engaged in performing worship upon the altar,
and who is adorned with various ornaments.
The fulfillment of all aspirations.
The all-pervading one, who possesses the ninefold true Dharma shaken forth by the Vinaya,
like the tips of all things stirred by the wind.
Resounding with the sound of banners and bells.
In the [four] cognitions, it is radiant with the mirror, the factors of enlightenment, the necklace, the half-necklace, the moon, the sun,
the mirror, the garland, and the chowrie.
This eightfold liberation is indeed like the eight maṇḍalas;
it accomplishes all attainments.
(Viṃśatividhi, Kriyāsamuccaya) HŪṂ Mahāsukha-vajrasattva! Come quickly, O Hūṃ Mahāsukha-vajrasattva! Come here swiftly!
O Mahāsukha Vajrasattva, come quickly! O Mahāsukha Vajrasattva, come quickly!
O Mahāsukha Vajra-Amogha!
The unerring commitment of the vajra of great bliss;
the equality of the vajra of great bliss and the unerring; the unerring commitment of the vajra of great bliss.
Protect!
Protect!
Protect!
Be pleasing to me, O Sugata;
be well-pleasing to me; be well-pleasing to me.
Be very firm for me;
be easy to nourish for me; be easy to sustain for me.
Be easy for me to nourish,
O Blessed One,
you who are a being without beginning or end, a being without beginning or end.
O Blessed One, being without beginning or end;
O Blessed One, being without beginning or end,
grant me all accomplishments— this is for you.
Having drawn in the being of Ma-tri-śa-ve-śya, one enters;
not by drawing it in, one enters.
Having drawn [them] forth, I cause them to enter;
bound by the pledges, I bring them under control. Having bound them by the pledges, I bring them under control.
Having bound them with the pledges, I bring them under control; having bound them with the pledges, I bring them under control—
by means of these steps of the mudrās.
Me! By means of these mudrās and mantra-words: Ḍza hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ.
jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ / jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ / jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ /
Great bliss, great passion, great vajra, great wealth,
great gnosis, great action.
O Vajrasattva and others, grant me accomplishments!
O Vajrasattva and others, grant me accomplishment!
O Primordial Great Being, O Great Joy, O Great Delight,
Samantabhadra, the Soul of All!
The Lord of Vajra-arrogance, the Lord.
O supreme concentration of the mind and being, O foremost concentration of the mind and being, O Vajra, great holder of the vajra!
Vajra-vajra, great wealth;
Samantabhadra, supreme conduct;
Samantabhadra, supreme conduct.
O Māra, O crusher of Māra!
O All-Enlightened One, Great Buddha,
born from the source of the foremost of Buddhas;
O Buddha, born from the source of the foremost of Buddhas.
Vajra-hūṃkāra hūṃkāra,
Vajra-hūṃkāra hūṃkāra, Vajra-hūṃkāra hūṃkāra.
O Lord of the World, bestower of jewels!
O Great Passion, O Great Bliss!
O Great Passion, O Great Bliss,
the great wealth of desire and liberation!
The foremost of the three times and the three worlds; the three times, the three worlds, and the foremost; the foremost of the three realms; and that which transcends the three elements.
The summit of the three worlds, the triple realm.
Manifested as originating from the immobile,
this manifestation arising from the immobile is a collection of both the extremely subtle and the gross.
The accumulation of the extremely subtle and the gross, the attainment of the most excellent among the mobile,
the purifier of the cycle of existence.
The purifier of the ocean of existence.
Since it is without beginning or end,
the entire primordial state (kāṇḍa), which is without beginning or end and absolute, has existed from the very outset.
O beloved, formerly everything was established; O beloved, formerly everything was situated;
O beloved, formerly everything was firmly established.
Heart-mudrā, the yoga-pledge; heart-mudrā, the yoga-pledge;
heart-mudrā, the yoga-pledge.
The great festival of the reality of truth.
Tathāgata Mahāsiddhi,
Tathāgata Mahāsiddha, Tathāgata Mahāsiddha.
The great Buddha of the Dharma-activity,
who brings about the easy realization of the thought of awakening (bodhicitta).
Vajra-anger, great anger, the one who binds with flames at the time of universal destruction;
O great discipliner of the foremost of the wicked!
O Rudra, O Rudra, the destroyer!
The great purity of all, the Great Lotus, the great method of wisdom and means,
the supreme samādhi of the purification of passion.
O Maheśvara, supreme in the samādhi of the purification of passion, supreme in the samādhi of the purification of passion, you who are the universal passion!
Truly, he is as eternal as the infinity of space;
truly, he is the great abode of all beings, infinite like space.
The great abode of all Buddhas.
O Lord, King of sovereign glory! O Lord, King of sovereign glory! O Lord, King of sovereign glory! O Lord, King!
It fulfills all aspirations.
Homage, homage! I am your devotee; let there be homage to you, homage, homage! I take refuge in you.
I am your devotee; I take refuge in you.
O Vajrasattva, grant me success this very day!
O Vajrasattva and others, grant me accomplishment!
Whoever daily recites this King of Hymns, or chants it even once with the voice of Dharma;
Success will be attained with ease.
Having praised [the deity] three times each day, every day, one who is liberated from all passion attains accomplishment in the pure fields.
By turning it even once, it constantly removes all suffering; it increases good fortune, prosperity, and wealth in all accomplishments.
Paramādya hūṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ.
Mahāsukha Vajrasattva,
I consecrate you with the consecration;
by means of this consecration, I consecrate you.
In the state of sovereignty over all vajras, be firm for me, be firm for me; grant me success!
Homage to you, O Blessed One, Mahāvajradhara!
Homage to you, O Blessed One, Mahāvajradhara! Mahāvajrasattva!
Mahāvajrasattva!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Having become heedless...
This water of hell shall burn you for transgressing the pledge;
through the preservation of the pledge, there is accomplishment.
Drink the water of the vajra-nectar.
Oṃ, I generate the bodhicitta of the supreme Mahāyoga of all Tathāgatas.
The protection and welfare of the entire realm of sentient beings, without exception or remainder.
The perfect accomplishment of the state of immortality,
great sovereignty and lordship, up to the supreme great siddhi of all.
And he intends for the sake of great wonder and splendor:
"The being without beginning or end is Vajrasattva, the Great Joy."
Samantabhadra, the self of all, the lord of Vajragarva, the Lord.
(Viṃśatividhi, Vajrāvalī):
Existence is indeed primordially pure by its very nature, O Paramādya.
That which has been rendered into non-existence by means of intrinsic natures is made into the supreme existence by virtuous beings who are pure in their intrinsic nature.
(Vajrāvalī) And being served with all enjoyments and articles of luxury as one pleases,
Through union with one's own presiding deity,
one should worship oneself (and likewise others).
Oṃ, primordial supreme one, O Vajra of Great Bliss! Oṃ, you who are consecrated as the Vajra, O Lord of all Vajras!
I consecrate you; I consecrate you,
O Great Vajra-holder.
O Mahāvajradhara! O Vajra! Salutation to the one named Vajra.
Salutation to the Siddhas.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ. O Primordial Supreme One!
O you who are firmly pleased, O you who are firmly satisfied, be well-pleased and well-nourished for me!
O Primordial One,
Vajra of All!
Vajra of All!
Oṃ! The syllable Ā is the gateway to all phenomena, because they are unarisen from the beginning.
Oṃ! The syllable Ākāra is the gateway to all phenomena, because they are unarisen from the beginning.
Oṃkāra is the mouth of all dharmas, because they are unarisen from the beginning.
O Supreme Primordial Lord of the World, for the sake of the perfect accomplishment of the enlightenment of the Buddhas!
Paramādya! Oṃ! Arise, O you who possess the great blazing vajra! Oṃ! Arise, O you who possess the greatly radiant vajra!
Quickly raise [him] up, HŪṂ!
Quickly raise [him] up, HŪṂ! Paramādya!
Oṃ, come, O Great Vajra-blazing-fire-sun!
Oṃ, come, O Great Vajra-blazing-fire-sun! Jaḥ!
O you who dwell within all vajra families, hūṃ!
Enter all the vajra families, HŪṂ! Bind all the hosts of mudrās, TRAṬ!
Bind all the hosts of mudrās, TRAṬ!
Accomplish all pledges, phaṭ! Accomplish all pledges, maṭ!
Burn all the wicked, cook them, reduce them to ashes!
Slay, burn, cook, and reduce all malevolent ones to ashes!
O Great Wrathful One, Wielder of the Fire-Vajra, hūṃ phaṭ! O Great Wrathful One, Wielder of the Fire-Vajra, hūṃ phaṭ!

Just as this red lotus is not stained by the defects of dye,
simply by beholding it...

Oṃ, purify, O pure one! Within the realm of sentient beings, within the entire accumulation of passion and so forth, within the accumulation of all passion and so forth.
I am piled up among all phenomena, O Vajra-accumulated one; I am piled up among all phenomena, O Conqueror of all phenomena, O Vajra-holder!
Oṃ, all Tathāgatas, Avalokiteśvara, Padma-hata! Ya.
Oṃ, to the Avalokiteśvara of all Tathāgatas, who holds a lotus in his hand; indeed, quickly [grant] me the vajra protection!
Indeed, quickly, having led these [beings] by means of the steps of the vajra-mudrās, having drawn them all forth and caused them to enter.
At this moment, I bind all beings; at this moment, I bring all under my control.
Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ.
Purify, accomplish all for me! Purify, accomplish all!
O Mahāvajradhara, stoṃ!
Padma, you are the Great Vajra-holder;
O Primordial Supreme One, oṃ siddha bhūṃ dhu!
Oṃ siddhya bhūḥ / siddhya bhuvaḥ / Siddha Mahāvajraratna!
Siddha Mahāvajraratna! Vā vāṭa ṭa traṃ! Va ca ṭa ṭa trāṃ!

VA VA GA GA SIDDHYA HOḤ TRĀṂ / Passion, hatred, and delusion are the primordial supreme.
These three,
when they have gone astray and are practiced in an unbalanced manner, surely attain the state of poison.
Furthermore, those who have cultivated immortality as immortality [attain] immortality.
(Tattvasiddhi, Caryāmelāpakapradīpa) Paramādya: Oṃ vajranārāyaṇa cinda pratihana vajracakreṇa hūṃ! Bhagavān Vajratathāgata!
Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ vajradhara taṃ / Vajratathāgata hūṃ / Oṃ vajranārāyaṇa cinda cinda / Apratihatavajrava(cakriṇa) hoḥ / Bhagavan vajratathāgata jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ / Vajratathāgata hūṃ //
O host of Vajra-wrath Great Yoginīs, essence of the assembly! Ho! O you who hold the great vajra-spear with fierce fangs! Bhagavān, to the Lord Vajracanḍeśvara! Ha ha ha ha hrīḥ!
O Lord of the host of Vajra-wrath Great Yoginīs! Hoḥ! O you who hold the great vajra-spike at the tip of your hand! Bhagavān!

Vajracaṇḍeśvara āḥ ha ha ha ha he / Vajrapadmobhava hoḥ / Bhagavān Vajralokeśvara Mahābrahme siddhya / Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ / Sasti nāma svāhā / Vajradhara hrīḥ / Vajrapadmodbhava hoḥ / Bhagavan Vajrāvalokiteśvara.

O Mahābrahmā, may there be success! Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Svasti namaḥ svāhā! O Vajrakusumāyudha, accomplish my purpose! Ho! Blessed One Vajrākāśagarbha, va va ta ta ṭra! O Vajrākāśagarbha, grant me everything! O Vajrakusumāyudha, accomplish all my desires! Ḥoḥ! Blessed One Vajrākāśagarbha, va va ṭa ṭa ṭrāṃ!

Homage to that truth by which the Blessed One is endowed with the Perfection of Wisdom; O Vajra-holder, O Discus-wielder! By that truth, [may] evil be [subdued]. Oṃ dhīḥ śrīḥ śruti smṛti vijaye svāhā. Vajra-armour! Homage to that truth by which the Blessed One is the Perfection of Wisdom; O Vajra-holder, O Discus-wielder! By that truth, [may] evil be [subdued]. Oṃ dhīḥ śrīḥ śroti smṛti vijaye svāhā.

Oṃ Vajragaurī, O Great Knowledge-Holder, Sovereign Victorious over the Three Worlds, Vajra-Anger, O One of the Fire-Samaya! O Vajra-Holder, homage be to you! It is as follows: Oṃ hilimili lelilāli vajrakārmukaye svāhā! Oṃ Vajragaurī, O Great Knowledge-Holder, Sovereign Victorious over the Three Worlds, Vajra-Anger, O One of the Fire-Samaya! O Vajra-Holder, let there be homage to you! It is as follows: hilemile lelilalirāli vajrakārmukaye svāhā!

By that truth by which, O Blessed One, you are named Vajrasamaya, the awakening of the Buddhas, the holder of the Buddhas; through the application of the Vajradharma, by that truth may I be accomplished! Oṃ tare tut tāre ture svāhā! Homage! By that truth by which, O Blessed Lady, there is the unsurpassed awakening of the Buddhas for those who apply themselves to the Vajradharma; by that truth may I be accomplished! Oṃ tāra tu tāre ture svāhā!

Oṃ! O Karmavajrī, you who have attained accomplishment, purify and bring about what is to be accomplished! O you born from space, through yoga, grant me accomplishment in the supreme act! It is thus: O you who are pure as space, you who fulfill all without exception, svāhā!

Oṃ! O Kāmavajrī, you are accomplished; you are pure! O Yoginī born from space, grant me accomplishment! You are the supreme syllable! It is thus: O you born from space, O you who are pure as space, you who fulfill all without exception, svāhā! O Primordial Supreme One!
Oṃ mahāsukha vajrasattva siddhi hūṃ!
Oṃ mahāsukhavajrasattva siddhya hūṃ!

jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. May he draw [them] together! O Great Pledge!

Bestower of the firm height of great bliss; bestower of the firm height of great bliss;

The primordial supreme: Oṃ; because it is the sign of the arising from space, it is supreme, without beginning or end.
O you who consist of the great vajra-being,
supreme among all, the great accomplishment, the presiding deity of great sovereignty!
May the King who holds all vajras grant me accomplishment in the supreme syllable.
You are faultless and eternal, O you who inspire passion for all passions;
O Great Passion, O Great Joy!
The Tathāgata is utterly pure, the foremost of all, liberated from the beginning;
he is Samantabhadra, the self of all.
The supreme among all, the great accomplishment,
the deity presiding over great sovereignty,
[is attained] by means of the mudrā of the pinnacle of great sovereignty.
O Siddhya, O Vajra, O Great Excellence, O Supreme Primordial One;
therefore, act according to your will.
He is the consumer of all and the doer of all;
he acts according to his will and moves about exactly as he desires upon the earth.
Whether standing, sitting, walking, or remaining as he is, [he is] the union of all Buddhas.
Whether laughing or conversing, wherever or in whatever manner.
The primordial supreme union of all Buddhas,
eternally abiding within the self of all.
The being who consists of all Buddhas is Vajrasattva, the supreme bliss.
The union of all Buddhas,
without beginning or end, is the Being, Vajrasattva, the Great Joy.
Samantabhadra is the self of all;
he is the Lord of Vajragarva, the Lord.
This Blessed One, the Self-Existent,
alone is the presiding deity of the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga*.

Primordial Supreme Oṃ! Oṃ, all Tathāgatas! Oṃ, all Tathāgatas!

Therefore, I consecrate you in the sovereignty of [the Buddha];
O Mahāvajradhara, Mahāvajradhara!
For you, too, must always maintain the vow of the Great Vajra-holder.
